title: wt removal result
description: The one document a wt removal prints in JSON mode, on success and on failure (nothing else goes to stdout). `items` is always present (`[]`, never null), one per item in the order wt acted on them; `dry_run` is always written (true: nothing was changed and every outcome says what a run would do). An item's `path` is ABSENT for a branch item and `ref` is ABSENT for a detached worktree; `saw` is the status the user saw when confirming; `worktree` and `branch` are the outcome enums (a branch item's `worktree` is `not_requested`); `reason` is one sanitised line (at most 200 characters, so it may be cut); `warnings` and `losses` are always arrays of sanitised lines (`losses`: what the engine's fresh re-check said removing it would lose; [] when nothing, or when it was refused before a re-check existed). `branch_tip` is the FULL 40-hex commit id of a branch this run deleted or may have deleted (deleted; deleted then restored because a worktree took it; deleted and not restored; git failed and the branch was gone): restore it with `git branch <name> <branch_tip>` while git keeps the commit. It is absent in a dry run and for every branch the run did not touch. On failure `error` is set (a nil error is reported as "unknown error"), `items` is empty and `dry_run` is false. Pinned to wt/internal/removal/json.go by wt/cmd/wt/remove_contract_test.go; an outcome or key added there must be added here and in remove-result.sample.json (or remove-result.dry-run.sample.json) in the same change.
